**The document does not report GPT-4 accuracy with 30 documents.** GPT-4 was only tested with 20 documents.

- **Limited GPT-4 testing:** The authors evaluated GPT-4 (8K) only "on a subset of multi-document QA experiments." They say running it on the full set of experiments "would cost upwards of $6000" (page 5, footnote 6).
- **20-document setting only:** GPT-4 was tested on "a subset of 500 random multi-document QA examples with 20 total documents in each input context" (page 15, Appendix D).
- **No GPT-4 row in the 30-document results:** The 30-document table (Table 7) includes only Claude-1.3, Claude-1.3 (100K), GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K), MPT-30B-Instruct and LongChat-13B (16K) (page 18).

**What the document does say about GPT-4 (20 documents):**
- It "achieves higher absolute performance than any other language model, but still shows a U-shaped performance curve." Accuracy is highest when the relevant document is at the very start or end of the context and drops when it is in the middle (page 15).
- No exact numbers are given in text. Reading Figure 15 by eye, accuracy is roughly 88% when the answer is in the 1st position, about 74–76% in the middle positions, and about 77% in the 20th position (page 15). These are estimates from the chart.
